question: Should outbound DM recipient allowlists be Slack-specific channel config, a shared human-chat channel policy, or folded into the broader message-tool outbound authorization model?
rationale: The code gap is clear, but adding `allowTo` creates a new public security/config contract and overlaps with broader outbound guardrail work, so automation should not choose the permanent policy boundary.

options.title: Shared outbound channel policy
options.body: Define a generic `allowTo`-style recipient policy for human-chat channels, then implement Slack first with docs and tests while leaving other channels to follow the same contract.

options.title: Slack-only first
options.body: Add `channels.slack.allowTo` now as a narrow defense-in-depth control, accepting a later migration if maintainers standardize outbound policy across channels.

options.title: Fold into broader guardrails
options.body: Track this as an acceptance case under https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87870 and defer the Slack-specific config until the broader policy is chosen.

recommendation.title: Shared outbound channel policy
recommendation.body: Define a generic `allowTo`-style recipient policy for human-chat channels, then implement Slack first with docs and tests while leaving other channels to follow the same contract.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest routing candidate because the original message tool and current Slack inbound policy boundary both trace to that history.
